profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.address: 5851 West Side Ave, North Bergen, NJ 07047
profile.reading:
Equinix's own facility page places this building, NY7, at 5851 West Side Avenue in North Bergen, New Jersey 07047, describing a three story, steel frame structure of 71,946 square feet. Published specifications list N+1 UPS redundancy, N+1 generator redundancy with 30 or more hours of autonomy at full load, N+2 cooling redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, and 120v/208v power distribution, with raised floors rated to 100 psf and slab to 175 psf. Certifications listed include HIPAA, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High, a certification set that differs from the ISO 22301/9001 and SOC 1 pairing Equinix publishes for NY3. Equinix advertises a 99.9999 percent plus global uptime guarantee and lists colocation, Equinix Internet Exchange, Metro Connect, Cross Connects, and Fabric services. No megawatt capacity figure and no year of construction are published on Equinix's own NY7 page.

North Bergen is a separate New Jersey municipality from Secaucus, and Equinix's own site treats NY7 as a standalone location rather than grouping it with the five building Secaucus cluster, NY2 through NY6, that sits roughly two to three miles away. Equinix's broader listing for its New York metro naming convention also includes NY1 in Newark, NY9, NY11 in Carteret, and NY13 further north in Elmsford, New York, all under the same regional brand despite being physically distinct sites in different towns and, in NY13's case, a different state. Data Center Frontier, a trade publication, reported in 2026 that this wider Equinix New York and New Jersey metro area totals nine IBX buildings and about 739,000 square feet of technical space in aggregate, without breaking that figure down site by site, and its detailed reporting on power infrastructure focused on the Secaucus campus's NY5 building rather than on NY7, so no comparable megawatt or generator count for NY7 itself was found in that reporting.

Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection company running more than 260 IBX data centers across more than 70 metro areas, converting to a real estate investment trust in 2015. Both Secaucus and North Bergen sit in Hudson County, roughly ten miles from Lower Manhattan, a location shaped by lower New Jersey real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor rather than by any single anchor tenant, though this registry has not found a source explaining why Equinix built NY7 in North Bergen specifically rather than adding a sixth building to the Secaucus cluster.

reading.body:
Equinix NY7 in North Bergen is a 71,946 square foot facility in New Jersey's Hudson County, part of Equinix's ten-building New York metro campus. The operator publishes no power capacity for this building, making its scale for AI workloads impossible to assess from available data. It maintains N+2 cooling redundancy, qualifying it for fault-tolerant hosted infrastructure, though this specification alone does not indicate whether the facility is sized or priced for AI training clusters.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities and only five with published power capacity totaling 111.3 megawatts, concentrated among a small number of operators. NY7 does not appear in the five published figures, placing it outside the state's disclosed capacity leaders despite its location in one of North America's densest infrastructure corridors.

Without published power capacity from Equinix, NY7 cannot be ranked against peers for AI infrastructure relevance. The absence of a disclosed megawatt figure across most regional facilities means this site's actual constraint on the grid, and therefore on AI scaling, remains unknown from public sources.
